Scratch

Working notes and derivations

Informal working notes — derivations in progress, ideas being chased down, and formulas parked here for reference.

Experiments That Stop Themselves

Some experiments have no predetermined number of trials: you repeat until some condition holds for the first time. The number of trials is then itself random, and the outcomes are sequences of variable length. The organising idea is to index outcomes by the trial n at which the process stops.

NoteFramework — Sequential Sample Space with a Stopping Rule

Let each trial produce a symbol from a finite alphabet \Sigma (e.g. \Sigma = \{H, T\}). Work inside the set of all finite strings \Sigma^\ast = \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \Sigma^k. A stopping rule designates, for each string, whether the process halts. The sample space is the set of strings that halt at their last symbol and at no earlier point: \Omega = \big\{\, \omega = \omega_1\cdots\omega_n \in \Sigma^\ast \;:\; \text{rule first satisfied at position } n \,\big\}. Grade \Omega by stopping time, \displaystyle \Omega = \bigsqcup_{n} \Omega_n where \Omega_n = \{\omega \in \Omega : |\omega| = n\}.

Since \Omega is countable, take \mathcal{F} = 2^{\Omega}, assign each outcome a probability, and verify \sum_{n} \sum_{\omega \in \Omega_n} \mathbb{P}(\{\omega\}) = 1. Any event about the process (“stops by trial 5”, “stops at an even trial”) is a union of the \Omega_n, so its probability is a sum — often a geometric series.

This is the same structure as any waiting-time problem (the geometric distribution: toss until the first head): don’t model the unbounded process directly, model “it took exactly n trials” and sum over n.

Worked Case — Toss Until the Same Result Twice in Succession

The rule halts at trial n when \omega_{n-1} = \omega_n, and this must be the first repeated adjacent pair — so \omega_1\cdots\omega_{n-1} strictly alternates.

NoteSample Space — Three Equivalent Forms

Direct (set-builder). \Omega = \Big\{\, \omega \in \{H,T\}^{n} \;:\; n \ge 2,\;\; \omega_i \neq \omega_{i+1}\ \text{for } 1 \le i \le n-2,\;\; \omega_{n-1} = \omega_n \,\Big\}. The alternation condition encodes “not stopped yet”; the last equality is the stop.

Graded by stopping time. \Omega = \bigsqcup_{n \ge 2} \Omega_n, \qquad |\Omega_n| = 2, because once \omega_1 \in \{H,T\} is chosen the whole string is forced (alternate for n-1 steps, then repeat).

Parametric. The map \omega \mapsto (\omega_1,\, |\omega|) is a bijection \Omega \;\longleftrightarrow\; \{H,T\} \times \{2, 3, 4, \dots\}.

NoteProbability Space

\Omega is countable, so \mathcal{F} = 2^{\Omega} and \mathbb{P} is fixed by its values on singletons, \mathbb{P}(\{\omega\}) = 2^{-|\omega|}, extended by countable additivity. This is a probability measure: \sum_{n \ge 2} |\Omega_n|\, 2^{-n} = \sum_{n \ge 2} 2 \cdot 2^{-n} = 1.

TipUnderlying model — stopping time on infinite sequences

Start from \tilde{\Omega} = \{H,T\}^{\mathbb{N}} with fair-coin product measure and define the stopping time N(\omega) = \min\{\, k \ge 2 \;:\; \omega_k = \omega_{k-1} \,\}. The finite-string \Omega above is the distribution of the truncated sequence (\omega_1, \dots, \omega_N), and \{N = n\} corresponds to \Omega_n.

First few strata

\begin{array}{rll} n = 2: & HH, & TT \\ n = 3: & THH, & HTT \\ n = 4: & HTHH, & THTT \\ & \vdots & \end{array}

Each stratum \Omega_n has two elements, each of probability 2^{-n}, so \mathbb{P}(\Omega_n) = 2^{1-n}.

## Experiments That Stop Themselves

Some experiments have no predetermined number of trials: you repeat until some condition holds for the first time. The number of trials is then itself random, and the outcomes are sequences of *variable length*. The organising idea is to **index outcomes by the trial $n$ at which the process stops**.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Framework — Sequential Sample Space with a Stopping Rule

Let each trial produce a symbol from a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ (e.g. $\Sigma = \{H, T\}$). Work inside the set of all finite strings
$$\Sigma^\ast = \bigcup_{k \ge 0} \Sigma^k.$$
A **stopping rule** designates, for each string, whether the process halts. The sample space is the set of strings that halt at their last symbol and at no earlier point:
$$\Omega = \big\{\, \omega = \omega_1\cdots\omega_n \in \Sigma^\ast \;:\; \text{rule first satisfied at position } n \,\big\}.$$
Grade $\Omega$ by stopping time, $\displaystyle \Omega = \bigsqcup_{n} \Omega_n$ where $\Omega_n = \{\omega \in \Omega : |\omega| = n\}$.

Since $\Omega$ is countable, take $\mathcal{F} = 2^{\Omega}$, assign each outcome a probability, and verify
$$\sum_{n} \sum_{\omega \in \Omega_n} \mathbb{P}(\{\omega\}) = 1.$$
Any event about the process ("stops by trial 5", "stops at an even trial") is a union of the $\Omega_n$, so its probability is a sum — often a geometric series.
:::

This is the same structure as any **waiting-time** problem (the geometric distribution: toss until the first head): don't model the unbounded process directly, model "it took exactly $n$ trials" and sum over $n$.

### Worked Case — Toss Until the Same Result Twice in Succession

The rule halts at trial $n$ when $\omega_{n-1} = \omega_n$, and this must be the *first* repeated adjacent pair — so $\omega_1\cdots\omega_{n-1}$ strictly alternates.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Sample Space — Three Equivalent Forms

**Direct (set-builder).**
$$
\Omega = \Big\{\, \omega \in \{H,T\}^{n} \;:\; n \ge 2,\;\; \omega_i \neq \omega_{i+1}\ \text{for } 1 \le i \le n-2,\;\; \omega_{n-1} = \omega_n \,\Big\}.
$$
The alternation condition encodes "not stopped yet"; the last equality is the stop.

**Graded by stopping time.**
$$
\Omega = \bigsqcup_{n \ge 2} \Omega_n, \qquad |\Omega_n| = 2,
$$
because once $\omega_1 \in \{H,T\}$ is chosen the whole string is forced (alternate for $n-1$ steps, then repeat).

**Parametric.** The map $\omega \mapsto (\omega_1,\, |\omega|)$ is a bijection
$$
\Omega \;\longleftrightarrow\; \{H,T\} \times \{2, 3, 4, \dots\}.
$$
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Probability Space

$\Omega$ is countable, so $\mathcal{F} = 2^{\Omega}$ and $\mathbb{P}$ is fixed by its values on singletons,
$$\mathbb{P}(\{\omega\}) = 2^{-|\omega|},$$
extended by countable additivity. This is a probability measure:
$$\sum_{n \ge 2} |\Omega_n|\, 2^{-n} = \sum_{n \ge 2} 2 \cdot 2^{-n} = 1.$$
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Underlying model — stopping time on infinite sequences

Start from $\tilde{\Omega} = \{H,T\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with fair-coin product measure and define the stopping time
$$N(\omega) = \min\{\, k \ge 2 \;:\; \omega_k = \omega_{k-1} \,\}.$$
The finite-string $\Omega$ above is the distribution of the truncated sequence $(\omega_1, \dots, \omega_N)$, and $\{N = n\}$ corresponds to $\Omega_n$.
:::

### First few strata

$$\begin{array}{rll}
n = 2: & HH, & TT \\
n = 3: & THH, & HTT \\
n = 4: & HTHH, & THTT \\
& \vdots &
\end{array}$$

Each stratum $\Omega_n$ has two elements, each of probability $2^{-n}$, so $\mathbb{P}(\Omega_n) = 2^{1-n}$.
